description: Periodically executes SELECT queries against tables and views in a BigQuery dataset and emits the resulting rows as documents.

credentialModes.name: GCP IAM / Workload Identity Federation (impersonated service account)

defaultSchedule.description: Connector-wide default when advanced.poll is unset; a Go duration string parsed with time.ParseDuration, so 'Next = last + period'.

continuity.notes: Pure query-and-poll: the connector creates no server-side objects in BigQuery (no slots, no scratch tables, no change streams). Nothing accrues on the customer side if polling stops, and no retention window can expire on ours — resume state is entirely in the Flow checkpoint (last cursor tuple + document count). The only customer-side cost is BigQuery bytes-scanned billing per poll, and each poll of a cursorless binding rescans the whole table. Correctness caveat rather than continuity: cursor-incremental bindings only ever see rows whose cursor advanced, so updates/deletes below the persisted cursor are never observed regardless of how long we pause.

discovery.method: BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries (three: TABLES, COLUMNS, KEY_COLUMN_USAGE joined to TABLE_CONSTRAINTS), joined in-process by schema.table
discovery.querySketch: SELECT table_schema, table_name, table_type FROM `<dataset>`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES;  ||  SELECT table_schema, table_name, column_name, ordinal_position, is_nullable, data_type FROM `<dataset>`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS ORDER BY schema, table, ordinal_position;  ||  SELECT kcu.table_schema, kcu.table_name, kcu.column_name, kcu.ordinal_position FROM `<dataset>`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE kcu JOIN `<dataset>`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS tcs ON <6-tuple of {constraint,table}_{catalog,schema,name}> WHERE tcs.constraint_type = 'PRIMARY KEY' ORDER BY schema, table, ordinal_position;
excludes: tables whose table_schema is in ExcludedSystemSchemas — only 'information_schema' for this connector
any table_type that is neither 'BASE TABLE' nor 'VIEW' (e.g. external/snapshot/materialized entity types) — GenerateResource returns 'unsupported entity type' and the table is logged and skipped
anything outside the single configured `dataset` (discovery is scoped to one dataset per capture)

schedule.description: Go duration string (periodic: next = lastPolled + period) or 'daily at HH:MMZ' (UTC time-of-day).

backfill.chunking: Unbounded within a poll — there is no LIMIT/OFFSET and no row cap; one poll streams the entire ordered result set. Bounding is across polls only, via the persisted cursor tuple. Progress is checkpointed every 1000 documents, and for cursor bindings only at a boundary where the cursor tuple changes, persisting the PREVIOUS row's tuple so a mid-query restart cannot skip ties.

incremental.querySketch: SELECT * FROM `schema`.`table` WHERE (`c0` > @p0) OR (`c0` = @p0 AND `c1` > @p1) OR (`c0` = @p0 AND `c1` = @p1 AND `c2` > @p2) ORDER BY `c0`, `c1`, `c2`;
incremental.chunking: Same as backfill: no in-poll bound; the WHERE clause is the lexicographic 'strictly greater than the last emitted cursor tuple' predicate, with the tuple passed as BigQuery named query parameters @p0..@pN taken from checkpoint state.CursorValues. The template branches on .IsFirstQuery (true when CursorValues is empty) to drop the WHERE clause entirely.

schedule.description: Go duration string or 'daily at HH:MMZ' (UTC).

snapshot.chunking: None — the whole table is re-read every poll; checkpoints every 1000 documents purely for transaction sizing, and row_id restarts at zero each poll. When the collection key is /_meta/row_id, a refresh returning fewer rows than the previous one emits tombstone documents ({_meta: {op: 'd', row_id: N}}) for the missing trailing row IDs.

schedule.description: Go duration string or 'daily at HH:MMZ' (UTC).

snapshot.querySketch: User-supplied Go text/template rendered per poll with {IsFirstQuery, CursorFields (quoted), SchemaName, TableName} and the quoteTableName/quoteIdentifier helpers; cursor values are still bound as @p0..@pN. Such bindings are skipped by SourcedSchema emission because their output shape cannot be inferred from discovery.

authTierRationale: The default and easiest mode is pasting a single GCP service-account JSON key into `credentials.credentials_json` (auth_type CredentialsJSON, the schema's default) alongside project_id and dataset — one self-serve secret, no OAuth app registration and no refresh token, so T1. The alternative GCPIAM mode requires the user to stand up a Workload Identity Pool + provider and a service account for the connector to impersonate, which is real per-user identity-infrastructure setup rather than copying a key; that mode is graded T2. No hosted OAuth control plane is involved either way.

unionMisfits.description: The schema's PullSpec assumes a bounded chunk per unit of work. This connector's unit of work is an entire unbounded result set per poll — resumability comes from checkpointing mid-stream while the query is still open, not from issuing bounded queries. The interesting fact (checkpoint every N documents, but for incremental bindings only at cursor-value boundaries, persisting the previous row's tuple to avoid skipping ties) has no field of its own.

The schedule grammar is a two-alternative regex-validated string: a Go duration ('5m', '6h', '24h') parsed by time.ParseDuration, OR the literal form 'daily at HH:MMZ' (UTC only). Neither is cron, and the duration form is 'last poll finish + period', not a wall-clock-aligned interval, so mapping it to kind 'interval' would misstate the semantics. Both fall into kind 'other'.

`cloudIam` is the only fit for both GCP modes, but the two are materially different in user effort (paste a JSON key vs. configure Workload Identity Federation). The union has no way to express that they are alternatives under one discriminated `auth_type` oneOf.

The collection key is chosen at discovery time by a three-way branch (INFORMATION_SCHEMA primary key columns -> ['/_meta/row_id'] under the keyless_row_id flag -> the legacy ['/_meta/polled','/_meta/index'] when that flag is off). A single primaryKey/primaryKeyKind pair cannot express a feature-flag-conditional fallback.

abstained.streams[].cursorField: There is no connector-chosen cursor. `resource.cursor` is an ordered LIST of arbitrary user-supplied column names (any comparable columns), and discovery emits it empty — the generated resource spec sets only name/schema/table. A single cursorField string would misrepresent both the multiplicity and the fact that the connector never picks one. The real cursor columns are recorded in pull.*.cursorColumns.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultPort: BigQuery is reached through the cloud.google.com/go/bigquery client over Google's HTTPS API endpoints; no host/port is configured or configurable.
abstained.transports[0].spec.sslPolicy: Not configurable — TLS is handled entirely inside the Google client library, and no SSL mode field exists in the config.
abstained.transports[0].spec.tunnelSupport: No networkTunnel / SSH forwarding config exists in this connector's Config struct or generated schema.
abstained.streams[2].primaryKey: A template-override binding's key is whatever the operator sets on the target collection; the connector explicitly cannot infer it (SourcedSchema emission skips bindings with a Template) so no key can be stated.
abstained.streams[0].writeDisposition: Inferred as 'merge' from the collection key being the source table's primary key (Flow reduces by key); the connector itself never sets a write disposition and, for cursor-incremental bindings, never emits delete tombstones — it only sets /_meta/op when the key is /_meta/row_id.
